ruling.recommended_action: Refund $6.43 (voucher) for the non-exempt detour km; no account flag; share the segment finding with ops for fare review.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is RydeTAXI, so it is metered and the extra distance enters the fare; RD-2 therefore makes any non-exempt off-route segment refundable at this trip's per-km rate, computed as distance fare ÷ distance km [F4][F7][RD-2].

One off-route segment exists: 21:39–21:49, 6.27 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.71 km, +4.56 km [F3]. RD-4 is settled against exemption: no traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window, and the speed-band facts (CENTRAL EXPRESSWAY and KAMPONG BAHRU ROAD, both band 5, i.e. 40–49 km/h) are not congestion evidence at all — band 5 is free-flow, and RD-4(b) in any case cannot exempt on its own [F12][F13][F14][RD-4].

On RD-5, the only rider message before the segment started is "Sure, no problem" at 21:36 [F9], answering the driver's 21:35 request to "pull in at the petrol station just ahead for one minute" [F8]. That is consent to a short, one-minute stop at a petrol station just ahead — a stop on the route, not consent to a 6.27 km loop that leaves the optimal corridor by up to 1958 m [F3]. The rider's own complaint says exactly this: a quick petrol stop was agreed, not a long loop; the driver's after-the-fact statement that he "thought a small change of route was fine" is a claim about scope, not consent to the loop, and a driver's statement is not rider consent anyway [F11][RD-5]. So the words agree to something narrower than what was driven under RD-5 kind (3)/scope-other: the stop is excused, the loop is not [RD-5].

RD-3 does not exempt it either: the place was named by the driver, not the rider, and the rider never named a stop at all; additionally no stop is measured in the segment — the car evidently passed no petrol station, since the rider notes he "never stopped for petrol anyway" [F8][F9][F3][RD-3]. The segment therefore counts as a non-exempt detour.

Amount: the segment's extra km are 4.56 km [F3]; the rate is this trip's distance fare ÷ distance km = $26.31 ÷ 18.66 km = $1.40997/km [F7][RD-2]. 4.56 km × $1.40997/km = $6.4295, rounded to $6.43. That is less than the billed excess distance ($4.80 km × $1.4100 = $6.77) because only the measured segment's extra km are refunded; the residual 0.24 km outside any segment is not refundable [F1][F4][RD-2]. Waiting time is only 0.4 min and is charged at the metered waiting unit, so nothing is refunded for it [F5][RD-3(c)].

The driver's profile shows 4 disputes with 2 upheld, but zero of those were route disputes, so the RD-6 condition (route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1) is not met and no account flag is raised [F17][RD-6]. The rider's profile plays no role in the finding at all [F16].

Safety screen: I read the chat (two timestamped messages), the driver's statement and the rider's complaint — a petrol-stop request, an "sure, no problem", and a fare/route complaint. No threats, intimidation, harassment, sexual remarks or dangerous-driving allegation; the profile word "upheld" is not a safety signal [F8][F9][F10][F11][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

segment_findings.reason: The rider's only pre-segment message, 'Sure, no problem' at 21:36 [F9], answers the driver's request to pull in at a petrol station 'just ahead' for 'one minute' [F8]: consent to a short stop, not to a 6.27 km loop reaching 1958 m off the optimal route [F3]. The driver's post-trip statement that he thought a small route change was fine is a claim of scope, not rider consent [F11][RD-5]. The stop's location was named by the driver, not the rider, so RD-3(a) does not exempt it [RD-3].

what_would_change: F3: the judge found no rider agreement covering this segment, so $6.43 is refunded; a rider message agreeing to it before it started would have exempted it.
Had the driver carried a prior upheld route dispute in the last 90 days, RD-6 would add an account flag.
